note: Chapter 1 part A (C00 to C03) from docs/chapter-01/CHAPTER_01_PRODUCTION.md section 5. Human lines are overheard; humans can't see or hear the spirits.

cloth_man.name: Man with a parcel of cloth

C00_morning.speaker: narrator
C00_morning.text: The bus is long gone. A woman with a basket walks straight at Reno.

C00_morning.speaker: narrator
C00_morning.text: Reno leaps aside. She walks on without a glance.

C00_morning.speaker: reno
C00_morning.text: I'm very visible. I'm wearing a red scarf.

C00_morning.speaker: narrator
C00_morning.text: A man cycles past and rings his bell at nothing in particular. Reno waves both arms. Nothing.

C00_morning.speaker: lumi
C00_morning.text: They can't see us. Or hear us.

C00_morning.speaker: reno
C00_morning.text: ...So I could make the funniest face in the world and nobody would know?

C00_morning.speaker: lumi
C00_morning.text: We need to get to Bandar Senja. Someone in this village must know the way. Maybe a spirit.

human_basket_woman.speaker: basket_woman
human_basket_woman.text: (to herself) Fish, kangkung, and... what else? Garlic. It's always the garlic.

human_basket_woman.speaker: lumi
human_basket_woman.text: She can't hear you, Reno. Stop waving.

C01_overheard.speaker: narrator
C01_overheard.text: Two voices drift over from the counter.

C01_overheard.speaker: kopitiam_owner
C01_overheard.text: (to a regular) The evening train from Bandar Senja always runs late.

C01_overheard.speaker: kopitiam_owner
C01_overheard.text: My cousin says people fall asleep on it and wake up not knowing where they are.

C01_overheard.speaker: regular
C01_overheard.text: Your cousin says a lot of things.

C01_overheard.speaker: reno
C01_overheard.text: Bandar Senja has a train! I knew it!

human_kopitiam_owner.speaker: kopitiam_owner
human_kopitiam_owner.text: (to herself) Who keeps moving my kettle? Every morning it's facing the door.

human_regular.speaker: regular
human_regular.text: (to his newspaper) Bus to Bandar Senja at nine. If it isn't late. It's always late.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: narrator
C01_old_kettle.text: A battered tin kettle on the back shelf opens one eye.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: old_kettle
C01_old_kettle.text: Forest kids, eh? Don't bother waving. They can't see you. They never could.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: old_kettle
C01_old_kettle.text: I'm a kettle with opinions. Thirty years on this shelf. I know every bus, every customer and every rumour in Sungai Melor.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: reno
C01_old_kettle.text: We need to get to Bandar Senja. For a train.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: old_kettle
C01_old_kettle.text: The bus will take you, if you can get on it. But first, do me a favour.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: old_kettle
C01_old_kettle.text: Something knocked Encik Lim's change jar over last night. A cold wind, out of nowhere. That's been happening a lot lately.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: old_kettle
C01_old_kettle.text: Veil wind. Sort his coins before he opens up, and I'll tell you the trick for the bus.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: old_kettle
C01_old_kettle.text: His sundry shop is next door. The back window doesn't latch.

C01_old_kettle.speaker: old_kettle
C01_old_kettle.text: Oh, and I keep a little shelf for spirit folk. Dewdrops only. Come back any time.

kettle_waiting.speaker: old_kettle
kettle_waiting.text: Coins first, forest kids. Encik Lim's shop is next door.

then.speaker: old_kettle
then.text: Suit yourselves.

then.speaker: old_kettle
then.text: Suit yourselves.

sundry_closed.speaker: narrator
sundry_closed.text: The sundry shop is shut. A card in the window says TUTUP.

sundry_closed.speaker: lumi
sundry_closed.text: Closed. Let's not go poking around in there for no reason.

C02_coin_jar_start.speaker: narrator
C02_coin_jar_start.text: Coins are spilled all over the floor of the closed shop: ones, fives, tens, twenties and a single fifty.

C02_coin_jar_start.speaker: lumi
C02_coin_jar_start.text: Old Kettle said piles of fifty cents.

C02_coin_jar_start.speaker: reno
C02_coin_jar_start.text: This one says ten. So five of these makes... a lot!

C02_coin_jar_solved.speaker: narrator
C02_coin_jar_solved.text: Four neat stacks of fifty cents. A key rattles in the front door.

C02_coin_jar_solved.speaker: narrator
C02_coin_jar_solved.text: Encik Lim opens up and stops dead.

C02_coin_jar_solved.speaker: encik_lim
C02_coin_jar_solved.text: (to himself) Sorted? All of it? ...I must have done it in my sleep.

coins_done.speaker: narrator
coins_done.text: The coins sit in four neat stacks. Encik Lim keeps counting them, just to be sure.

C02_kettle_reward.speaker: old_kettle
C02_kettle_reward.text: Sorted, all of it! Lim's been staring at those stacks for ten minutes. Here, for your trouble.

C02_kettle_reward.speaker: narrator
C02_kettle_reward.text: Old Kettle tips a few Dewdrops and two slices of kaya toast off the shelf. "They fell off a plate."

C02_kettle_reward.speaker: old_kettle
C02_kettle_reward.text: Now, the bus trick. Wait for someone with a big load. The door stays open longest for people carrying baskets.

C02_kettle_reward.speaker: old_kettle
C02_kettle_reward.text: And ride up top, on the luggage rack. Nobody sits there.

C02_kettle_reward.speaker: reno
C02_kettle_reward.text: The luggage rack! Like real travellers!

C02_kettle_reward.speaker: lumi
C02_kettle_reward.text: Real travellers sit in seats, Reno.

C02_kettle_reward.speaker: old_kettle
C02_kettle_reward.text: The stop is east of the village, down the main road. Good luck, forest kids.

bus_no_plan.speaker: narrator
bus_no_plan.text: The bus door wheezes open for a passenger, then snaps shut.

bus_no_plan.speaker: lumi
bus_no_plan.text: It closes too fast. Old Kettle said he knows every bus. Let's ask him first.

human_rambutan_man.speaker: rambutan_man
human_rambutan_man.text: (to himself) Two baskets of rambutans for my sister in Bandar Senja. The driver always grumbles, but he waits.

human_queue_a.speaker: passenger_a
human_queue_a.text: (to the woman behind him) Just a small bag today. In and out, quick as anything.

human_queue_b.speaker: passenger_b
human_queue_b.text: (to the man in front) Is it nine already? This bus has never once been on time.

C03_boarding.speaker: narrator
C03_boarding.text: The bus doors wheeze open. The queue shuffles forward. Who do you follow on?

choice.text: The man with a small bag

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: You slip in behind the man with the small bag. The door snaps shut right behind them, in front of your noses.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Too quick. Old Kettle said someone with a big load keeps the door open longest.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: The driver opens the door again for the next in the queue. There's still time.

choice.text: The man with two big baskets

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: He heaves two huge baskets of rambutans up the step. The driver sighs and waits, and waits.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Now!

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Reno Leaf Leaps over the baskets and onto the luggage rack. Lumi floats up after him.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: You slip in behind the woman with the parasol. The door snaps shut right behind them, in front of your noses.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Too quick. Old Kettle said someone with a big load keeps the door open longest.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: The driver opens the door again for the next in the queue. There's still time.

C03_bus_ride.speaker: narrator
C03_bus_ride.text: The bus rattles along the river road.

C03_bus_ride.speaker: reno
C03_bus_ride.text: (on the luggage rack, nose against the window) It's even better than I imagined.

C03_bus_ride.speaker: lumi
C03_bus_ride.text: You're lying on a sack of onions.

C03_bus_ride.speaker: passenger_a
C03_bus_ride.text: My brother at the station says three parcels have gone missing this week.

C03_bus_ride.speaker: passenger_a
C03_bus_ride.text: And the goods shed is full of moths.

C03_bus_ride.speaker: narrator
C03_bus_ride.text: Far away, a train whistle sounds. Not one passenger looks up.

C03_bus_ride.speaker: reno
C03_bus_ride.text: The bus going brrrrrm? Yes! It's the best sound in the world!

C03_arrival.speaker: narrator
C03_arrival.text: Bandar Senja. The bus coughs to a stop in front of a real railway station.

C03_arrival.speaker: reno
C03_arrival.text: Lumi. LUMI. Look at the clock tower!

C03_arrival.speaker: lumi
C03_arrival.text: Missing parcels, moths, a train that makes people forget... I don't like this, Reno.

human_fisherman.speaker: fisherman
human_fisherman.text: (to himself) Where did my postcard go? My sister in Bandar Senja will think I forgot her again.

C01_S01_postcard.speaker: narrator
C01_S01_postcard.text: A postcard lies face down on the jetty planks, already stamped.

C01_S01_postcard.speaker: lumi
C01_S01_postcard.text: It's the fisherman's. It's addressed to Bandar Senja.

C01_S01_postcard.speaker: reno
C01_S01_postcard.text: We're going there! We can post it for him.

mr_slot.speaker: mr_slot
mr_slot.text: Letters, postcards, small parcels. In my mouth, out to the world. That's the job.

mr_slot.speaker: mr_slot
mr_slot.text: I'm THE post box. Mr Slot. Forty years on this corner and never lost a letter.

mr_slot_postcard.speaker: lumi
mr_slot_postcard.text: Mr Slot, could you take this? A fisherman in Sungai Melor dropped it.

mr_slot_postcard.speaker: mr_slot
mr_slot_postcard.text: A postcard home! My favourite kind. In it goes.

mr_slot_postcard.speaker: narrator
mr_slot_postcard.text: The postcard drops into the slot with a happy little clunk.

mr_slot_postcard.speaker: mr_slot
mr_slot_postcard.text: His sister will have it by Thursday. Here, a little something for honest couriers.

mr_slot_after.speaker: mr_slot
mr_slot_after.text: Thursday, I said. I'm never late. Unlike some trains I could mention.

C04_overheard.speaker: narrator
C04_overheard.text: A tired voice rises over the clatter of the hall.

C04_overheard.speaker: pak_darus
C04_overheard.text: (to the ticket clerk) Three parcels gone. One somewhere in the goods shed, one in the yard, and one sent to the wrong shop with a label nobody can read.

C04_overheard.speaker: pak_darus
C04_overheard.text: If they're not on my desk by tonight, head office will have my cap.

C04_overheard.speaker: ticket_clerk
C04_overheard.text: Maybe the moths ate them, Pak.

C04_overheard.speaker: pak_darus
C04_overheard.text: Don't joke. Not about the moths.

human_pak_darus.speaker: pak_darus
human_pak_darus.text: (to his paperwork) Parcel A, parcel B, parcel C. Gone, gone and gone. Wonderful.

human_ticket_clerk.speaker: ticket_clerk
human_ticket_clerk.text: (to herself) Evening train delayed again. I'll just write "late" on the board and save the chalk.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: narrator
C04_clockkeeper.text: A ticking voice comes from the big station clock above the ticket window.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: Tick. You two. Yes, you. The ones he can't see.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: The clock has been talking since 1931. Nobody listens. Tick. You want the evening train?

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: Then you need one of my tickets. Stamped for the Veil. The evening train hasn't been running straight for weeks.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: Board it without a stamp, and you may not get off where you meant to.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: lumi
C04_clockkeeper.text: And what do you want in return?

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: Pak Darus is a good man. He winds me every Monday. Find his parcels and put them on his desk. Quietly.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: Wait until he looks away before you put anything down. Humans notice a parcel appearing under their nose.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: The goods shed is west of the forecourt. Shophouse Row is east. The yard is through that door. Tick.

C04_clockkeeper.speaker: clockkeeper
C04_clockkeeper.text: And I keep a shelf of travel snacks. Dewdrops, if you have them.

then.speaker: clockkeeper
then.text: Tick.

then.speaker: clockkeeper
then.text: Tick.

C08_tickets.speaker: clockkeeper
C08_tickets.text: All three, back on his desk. He's been smiling at them for an hour. Tick.

C08_tickets.speaker: narrator
C08_tickets.text: The Clockkeeper's hands spin. Two tickets drop from his case, each stamped with a violet tick mark.

C08_tickets.speaker: clockkeeper
C08_tickets.text: Carriage three. Keep these on you. And if the train runs late, don't blame me. That one always does.

C08_tickets.speaker: lumi
C08_tickets.text: Platform 2 is through the north door. The evening train comes at dusk.

yard_not_yet.speaker: lumi
yard_not_yet.text: The rail yard's through there. Let's find out what's going on in this station first.

platform_not_yet.speaker: lumi
platform_not_yet.text: Platform 2. We can't board without the Clockkeeper's tickets.

desk_idle.speaker: narrator
desk_idle.text: The stationmaster's desk. Forms, stamps, a cold cup of coffee and a lot of empty space where three parcels should be.

parcel_reaction.speaker: pak_darus
parcel_reaction.text: Ticket clerk! Did you... never mind. Never mind.

parcel_reaction.speaker: lumi
parcel_reaction.text: That's all three! Let's tell the Clockkeeper.

parcel_reaction.speaker: pak_darus
parcel_reaction.text: I'm not going to question it.

place_parcel_a.speaker: narrator
place_parcel_a.text: Quick, while he's turned away: Reno slides the parcel onto the desk.

place_parcel_a.speaker: narrator
place_parcel_a.text: Pak Darus turns back around and freezes.

place_parcel_b.speaker: narrator
place_parcel_b.text: Quick, while he's turned away: Reno slides the parcel onto the desk.

place_parcel_b.speaker: narrator
place_parcel_b.text: Pak Darus turns back around and freezes.

place_parcel_c.speaker: narrator
place_parcel_c.text: Quick, while he's turned away: Reno slides the parcel onto the desk.

place_parcel_c.speaker: narrator
place_parcel_c.text: Pak Darus turns back around and freezes.

C05_shed.speaker: narrator
C05_shed.text: Crates everywhere. Something dusty rolls between the aisles.

C05_shed.speaker: lumi
C05_shed.text: There's a parcel on the top shelf at the back. But the aisle is blocked.

C05_shed.speaker: reno
C05_shed.text: Root Grip! I'll just pull every crate at once.

C05_shed.speaker: lumi
C05_shed.text: One crate at a time. And not onto my foot.

C05_shed.speaker: narrator
C05_shed.text: Hint: face a crate as Reno and press A to pull it one tile toward you. The lever by the door puts every crate back.

grip_lumi.speaker: lumi
grip_lumi.text: Root Grip is Reno's trick. I'd only scratch the paint.

grip_no_room.speaker: reno
grip_no_room.text: Nnngh! There's no room behind me to pull it.

shed_reset.speaker: narrator
shed_reset.text: A big lever marked RESET. Pull it?

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: Clank! Something in the roof whirs, and every crate slides back to where it started.

C05_parcel_a.speaker: narrator
C05_parcel_a.text: Behind the crates, on the back shelf: a parcel with the station's stamp.

C05_parcel_a.speaker: lumi
C05_parcel_a.text: Now it goes on Pak Darus's desk. While he isn't looking.

shelf_empty.speaker: narrator
shelf_empty.text: The back shelf. Just dust now.

C05_dead_letter_look.speaker: narrator
C05_dead_letter_look.text: A high shelf marked DEAD LETTERS. One parcel tag says 1951. Its emblem looks just like Reno's railway token.

C05_dead_letter_look.speaker: reno
C05_dead_letter_look.text: Lumi, could you do your touchy thing on it?

C05_dead_letter_look.speaker: narrator
C05_dead_letter_look.text: (Swap to Lumi with C, then look again.)

C05_dead_letter_touch.speaker: narrator
C05_dead_letter_touch.text: Lumi rests her fingers on the 1951 tag. The shed goes quiet.

C05_dead_letter_touch.speaker: narrator
C05_dead_letter_touch.text: Footsteps on a platform. A woman's voice: "Mind the gap, little one."

C05_dead_letter_touch.speaker: lumi
C05_dead_letter_touch.text: Someone in 1951 had the same one.

dead_letter_done.speaker: narrator
dead_letter_done.text: The 1951 tag. Lumi doesn't want to touch it again just yet.

dust_b_beaten.speaker: lumi
dust_b_beaten.text: Veil creatures, in a human goods shed. The Veil is thin here.

C06_label_reno.speaker: narrator
C06_label_reno.text: A delivery note is pinned to the noticeboard: PARCEL C. The address is a smudge.

C06_label_reno.speaker: reno
C06_label_reno.text: It says... blob. Blob street, number blob.

C06_label_reno.speaker: lumi
C06_label_reno.text: Let me try. Things remember where they were meant to go.

C06_label_reno.speaker: narrator
C06_label_reno.text: (Swap to Lumi with C, then look again.)

C06_memory_touch.speaker: narrator
C06_memory_touch.text: Lumi touches the smudged label. Memory Touch!

C06_memory_touch.speaker: narrator
C06_memory_touch.text: Something BLUE. A ROUND shape on a signboard. The letters ...CLE.

C06_memory_touch.speaker: lumi
C06_memory_touch.text: Things remember where they were meant to go.

C06_memory_touch.speaker: reno
C06_memory_touch.text: Does my satchel remember where my lunch went?

C06_memory_touch.speaker: lumi
C06_memory_touch.text: Your satchel remembers you ate it.

C06_memory_touch.speaker: lumi
C06_memory_touch.text: Blue, round, ...CLE. Let's check the shop signs along the row.

label_again.speaker: narrator
label_again.text: The smudged note. Lumi's fragments: something BLUE, a ROUND shape, and ...CLE.

sign_tailor.speaker: narrator
sign_tailor.text: A red signboard with a pair of scissors: TAILOR.

sign_bicycle.speaker: narrator
sign_bicycle.text: A blue signboard with a big wheel: BICYCLE REPAIR.

sign_photo.speaker: narrator
sign_photo.text: A green signboard with a camera: PHOTO STUDIO.

sign_gold.speaker: narrator
sign_gold.text: A gold signboard with a ring: GOLDSMITH.

pz105_tailor.speaker: narrator
pz105_tailor.text: A red signboard with a pair of scissors: TAILOR.

pz105_tailor.speaker: reno
pz105_tailor.text: Scissors are round-ish. When they're open. Sort of.

pz105_tailor.speaker: lumi
pz105_tailor.text: It's red, Reno. And there's no ...CLE.

pz105_photo.speaker: narrator
pz105_photo.text: A green signboard with a camera: PHOTO STUDIO.

pz105_photo.speaker: reno
pz105_photo.text: The camera has a round bit!

pz105_gold.speaker: narrator
pz105_gold.text: A gold signboard with a ring: GOLDSMITH.

pz105_gold.speaker: reno
pz105_gold.text: A ring is round! And shiny!

C06_parcel_c.speaker: narrator
C06_parcel_c.text: A blue signboard with a big wheel: BICYCLE REPAIR. Blue, round, biCYCLE.

C06_parcel_c.speaker: narrator
C06_parcel_c.text: Inside, among inner tubes and spanners, sits a parcel with the station's stamp.

C06_parcel_c.speaker: narrator
C06_parcel_c.text: Reno pokes a bicycle wheel on the way out. It spins.

C06_parcel_c.speaker: repairer
C06_parcel_c.text: (to himself, looking up) Wind's strange today.

C06_parcel_c.speaker: lumi
C06_parcel_c.text: It's a bicycle. And he can't hear you ask.

human_repairer.speaker: repairer
human_repairer.text: (to himself) Who sends a parcel to a bicycle shop? I don't even sign for parcels.

C07_yard.speaker: narrator
C07_yard.text: Ticket Moths flutter over the rails, carrying scraps of paper toward a fenced siding in the north-east.

C07_yard.speaker: lumi
C07_yard.text: Look. They're all flying to that siding. And there's something wrapped up in there.

C07_yard.speaker: lumi
C07_yard.text: The siding gate is shut. That handcar could knock it open, if the signals sent it the right way.

C07_yard.speaker: narrator
C07_yard.text: Hint: the three levers switch the points. Lumi's Echo Sight can show the old marker's memory.

lever_1.speaker: narrator
lever_1.text: Clunk. Signal lever 1 is now SWITCHED.

lever_1.speaker: narrator
lever_1.text: Clunk. Signal lever 1 is now STRAIGHT.

lever_2.speaker: narrator
lever_2.text: Clunk. Signal lever 2 is now SWITCHED.

lever_2.speaker: narrator
lever_2.text: Clunk. Signal lever 2 is now STRAIGHT.

lever_3.speaker: narrator
lever_3.text: Clunk. Signal lever 3 is now SWITCHED.

lever_3.speaker: narrator
lever_3.text: Clunk. Signal lever 3 is now STRAIGHT.

PZ104_marker_reno.speaker: narrator
PZ104_marker_reno.text: An old stone marker by the rails, worn smooth.

PZ104_marker_reno.speaker: reno
PZ104_marker_reno.text: Lumi, you see echoes. Want to look?

PZ104_marker_reno.speaker: narrator
PZ104_marker_reno.text: (Swap to Lumi with C, then look again.)

PZ104_echo.speaker: narrator
PZ104_echo.text: Echo Sight! A ghostly handcar glides past, the last one that ever made it to the siding.

PZ104_echo.speaker: narrator
PZ104_echo.text: At lever 1 it turns. At lever 2 it goes straight on. At lever 3 it turns.

PZ104_wrong.speaker: narrator
PZ104_wrong.text: Reno gives the handcar a shove. It rattles off down the rails...

PZ104_wrong.speaker: narrator
PZ104_wrong.text: ...and rolls back a minute later, the wrong way round.

PZ104_wrong.speaker: lumi
PZ104_wrong.text: The points sent it somewhere else. Let's check the levers.

PZ104_solved.speaker: narrator
PZ104_solved.text: Reno gives the handcar a shove. It rattles off, clatters through all three points and slams into the siding gate.

PZ104_solved.speaker: narrator
PZ104_solved.text: The gate bursts open. Paper scraps snow down over the yard.

PZ104_solved.speaker: lumi
PZ104_solved.text: Now there's only the nest. And whatever made it.

moths_beaten.speaker: reno
moths_beaten.text: They were carrying bits of tickets!

flicker_beaten.speaker: lumi
flicker_beaten.text: A signal lamp that came alive. The Veil really is thin here.

C07_monarch_intro.speaker: narrator
C07_monarch_intro.text: The nest heaves. A huge moth unfolds, its wings made of chewed tickets.

C07_monarch_intro.speaker: monarch
C07_monarch_intro.text: Mine. All the little papers that say where... mine.

C07_monarch_intro.speaker: reno
C07_monarch_intro.text: It's eating tickets! That's the worst crime I can think of!

C07_monarch_intro.speaker: lumi
C07_monarch_intro.text: Why would a moth want destinations?

C07_monarch_outro.speaker: narrator
C07_monarch_outro.text: The Monarch crumples into a heap of paper. Inside the nest: Parcel B, and a punched ticket with no destination printed on it. Just a neat hole.

C07_monarch_outro.speaker: lumi
C07_monarch_outro.text: Someone is collecting where people are going.

C07_monarch_outro.speaker: reno
C07_monarch_outro.text: Then they'd better not touch our tickets.

C07_monarch_outro.speaker: narrator
C07_monarch_outro.text: Got Parcel B, the Blank Punched Ticket and the Moth-Wing Charm. (Lumi wears the charm: SPD +2.)

C07_monarch_outro.speaker: narrator
C07_monarch_outro.text: New team skill: Guardian Bloom! Reno and Lumi use both turns and 5 MP each to shield each other (damage x0.7 for 2 turns) and heal 15% of their HP. Find it under Bloom in battle.

C08_board.speaker: narrator
C08_board.text: Platform 2 at dusk. The evening train pulls in, hissing steam.

C08_board.speaker: narrator
C08_board.text: They slip aboard behind a porter. A fog rolls across the platform.

C08_board.speaker: narrator
C08_board.text: The lamps turn from yellow to blue-violet, and the station clock runs backwards for one tick.

C09_carriage.speaker: narrator
C09_carriage.text: Passengers sit staring forward. Each holds a ticket with a neat hole where the destination should be.

C09_carriage.speaker: narrator
C09_carriage.text: Pale moths drift between the seats, carrying faint glowing slips.

C09_carriage.speaker: lumi
C09_carriage.text: Reno. We're inside the Veil. The whole train is.

passengers_check.speaker: narrator
passengers_check.text: Far down the train, a whistle blows. A door clanks open somewhere past the luggage van.

passengers_check.speaker: lumi
passengers_check.text: The Guard's Van. Whoever is taking the destinations is in there.

C09_teacher.speaker: teacher
C09_teacher.text: Are you... a dream? I'm going... I was going... somewhere with a blackboard?

C09_teacher.speaker: lumi
C09_teacher.text: Only a little. Like when you're half asleep.

C09_teacher.speaker: lumi
C09_teacher.text: They haven't lost their luggage. They've lost where they were going.

C09_teacher.speaker: narrator
C09_teacher.text: A box of new chalk sits on her lap. Which slip do you offer?

choice.text: The slip that smells of chalk

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: The slip melts into her ticket. A destination appears where the hole was.

then.speaker: teacher
then.text: Kampung Seri Pagi. My first school. Forty children and one blackboard. I'm going to be late!

then.speaker: reno
then.text: Good luck, teacher!

choice.text: The slip with a baby's laugh

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: No... that one doesn't fit. It flutters back to us.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: No... that one doesn't fit. It flutters back to us.

teacher_after.speaker: teacher
teacher_after.text: (half asleep) Forty children... I'll learn every name.

C09_grandmother.speaker: grandmother
C09_grandmother.text: Such polite little dreams. I'm knitting for someone, but I can't think who...

C09_grandmother.speaker: narrator
C09_grandmother.text: A pair of tiny yellow booties hangs off her needles. Which slip do you offer?

choice.text: The slip that smells of chalk

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: No... that one doesn't fit. It flutters back to us.

choice.text: The slip with a baby's laugh

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: The slip settles on the booties. She smiles all the way up to her eyes.

then.speaker: grandmother
then.text: My grandson! He was born on Tuesday. I'm going to meet him.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: He's going to love the booties.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: No... that one doesn't fit. It flutters back to us.

grandmother_after.speaker: grandmother
grandmother_after.text: (half asleep) Tuesday. Born on a Tuesday...

C09_cloth_man.speaker: cloth_man
C09_cloth_man.text: Blue for the shirt, or was it... I had a reason to carry all this. Didn't I?

C09_cloth_man.speaker: narrator
C09_cloth_man.text: He hugs a parcel of folded batik. Which slip do you offer?

choice.text: The slip that smells of chalk

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: No... that one doesn't fit. It flutters back to us.

choice.text: The slip with a baby's laugh

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: No... that one doesn't fit. It flutters back to us.

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: We don't have that one yet.

then.speaker: narrator
then.text: The slip slides into the folds of the cloth.

then.speaker: cloth_man
then.text: The tailor on Jalan Pasar! My daughter's wedding shirt. Of course.

then.speaker: reno
then.text: A wedding! Will there be cake?

then.speaker: lumi
then.text: Reno.

cloth_man_after.speaker: cloth_man
cloth_man_after.text: (half asleep) Wedding shirt. Blue. Mustn't crease it.

vt01_moths_beaten.speaker: narrator
vt01_moths_beaten.text: The Memory Moths dissolve into light. One glowing slip is left. It smells of chalk dust.

C09_dining.speaker: narrator
C09_dining.text: The dining car. Tea cups rattle. Nobody drinks.

C09_dining.speaker: lumi
C09_dining.text: More passengers. Look at what they're holding. It might tell us which slip is whose.

vt02_moth_beaten.speaker: narrator
vt02_moth_beaten.text: A glowing slip drifts down. It hums with a baby's laugh.

C09_roof.speaker: narrator
C09_roof.text: The roof of the train. The Veil sky streams past, violet and full of stars.

C09_roof.speaker: reno
C09_roof.text: There's a slip up here! Past the gaps between the carriages.

C09_roof.speaker: narrator
C09_roof.text: Hint: face a gap as Reno and press A to Leaf Leap. A miss just puts you back where you were.

C09_float_unlock.speaker: narrator
C09_float_unlock.text: The last gap is far too wide to jump.

C09_float_unlock.speaker: lumi
C09_float_unlock.text: I think I can float across.

C09_float_unlock.speaker: reno
C09_float_unlock.text: This is the best day of my life.

C09_float_unlock.speaker: lumi
C09_float_unlock.text: We're on the roof of a ghost train.

C09_float_unlock.speaker: narrator
C09_float_unlock.text: Lumi learned Gentle Float! Swap to Lumi with C, face a wide gap and press A. Reno holds on.

slip_cloth_pickup.speaker: narrator
slip_cloth_pickup.text: A glowing slip, caught on a roof vent. It feels like soft new cloth.

guards_van_locked.speaker: narrator
guards_van_locked.text: A heavy door marked GUARD. It won't budge.

guards_van_locked.speaker: lumi
guards_van_locked.text: Not yet. The passengers need their destinations back first.

vt04_porter_beaten.speaker: reno
vt04_porter_beaten.text: Even the luggage handlers are made of fog in here.

trunk_plain.speaker: narrator
trunk_plain.text: An old steamer trunk with a brass lock.

PZ108_keyhole.speaker: narrator
PZ108_keyhole.text: Lumi holds up the lantern from Kampung Akar. In its light, a second keyhole glows on the trunk, violet and very much not brass.

PZ108_keyhole.speaker: narrator
PZ108_keyhole.text: The trunk shudders, hops off the pile... and lands right beside you, lid snapping.

PZ108_keyhole.speaker: lumi
PZ108_keyhole.text: Lost luggage. Nobody claimed it, so it got grumpy.

trunk_open.speaker: narrator
trunk_open.text: The trunk's Veil keyhole has faded.

lost_luggage_outro.speaker: narrator
lost_luggage_outro.text: The Lost Luggage settles down with a contented creak. Something brass rolls out of it.

lost_luggage_outro.speaker: narrator
lost_luggage_outro.text: Got the Brass Lantern Hook. (Lumi carries it: MAG +3.)

C10_conductor.speaker: narrator
C10_conductor.text: A tall, thin figure in a faded uniform, with a lantern for a face. His cap badge has been rubbed blank.

C10_conductor.speaker: narrator
C10_conductor.text: He reaches for their tickets, and recoils from the Clockkeeper's violet stamp.

C10_conductor.speaker: conductor
C10_conductor.text: Stamped. Stamped tickets. Then I cannot take your where. Tickets, please. Where are you going?

C10_conductor.speaker: reno
C10_conductor.text: Bandar... no, wait, we're already... somewhere fun!

C10_conductor.speaker: conductor
C10_conductor.text: Everyone is going somewhere. I am going nowhere. I had a name once. It was on a list. Now there is no list.

C10_conductor.speaker: conductor
C10_conductor.text: So I keep everyone's where... so I am not alone with my nowhere.

C10_ticket.speaker: narrator
C10_ticket.text: The Conductor sways. Lumi steps forward with the blank punched ticket from the moth nest.

C10_ticket.speaker: narrator
C10_ticket.text: Memory Touch. The ticket remembers one thing that is still his: a small platform at dawn, and a man in a uniform waving passengers off.

C10_ticket.speaker: reno
C10_ticket.text: You still can! You just took a wrong turn. I do that constantly.

C10_ticket.speaker: narrator
C10_ticket.text: The train slows. Outside, a platform appears under a violet sky.

C11_veil_halt.speaker: narrator
C11_veil_halt.text: The Veil Halt. The Conductor opens his lantern, and hundreds of small lights drift back into the carriages.

C11_veil_halt.speaker: narrator
C11_veil_halt.text: One light doesn't go to any passenger. It drifts to Lumi. A lullaby, the one from Reno's dream, and a voice: "Remember the way home."

C11_veil_halt.speaker: lumi
C11_veil_halt.text: I don't think I lost it. I think I never had it. There's nothing before... before I woke up in Kampung Akar.

C11_veil_halt.speaker: conductor
C11_veil_halt.text: (reading an old ledger) Your name is here, little echo. But nothing is written before it. As if you began in the middle of a sentence.

C11_veil_halt.speaker: reno
C11_veil_halt.text: Then you get to write the rest. That's the fun part.

C11_veil_halt.speaker: narrator
C11_veil_halt.text: The Conductor gives Reno his whistle and points down the platform, to steps that lead into mist and the sound of water.

C11_veil_halt.speaker: conductor
C11_veil_halt.text: The rails forget. The river remembers. If someone is taking names, the river spirits will know who.

C11_veil_halt.speaker: conductor
C11_veil_halt.text: I will keep this halt until mine is written again.

conductor_halt.speaker: conductor
conductor_halt.text: The river remembers. Go well, little travellers.

C11_dawn.speaker: narrator
C11_dawn.text: Dawn at Platform 2. The train is an ordinary train again. Passengers wake up yawning.

C11_dawn.speaker: teacher
C11_dawn.text: (to the woman beside her) I had the strangest dream. Two children on the roof of the train.

C11_dawn.speaker: pak_darus
C11_dawn.text: (to himself) Late again. But everyone's here. Strange.

C11_dawn.speaker: narrator
C11_dawn.text: Above the platform, the Clockkeeper ticks once, pleased.

C11_dawn.speaker: reno
C11_dawn.text: Lumi, can we ride another one?
